method.method_draft: First identify from the figure that closing S directly connects the two capacitor top nodes while the bottom nodes are already common, so after t=0 the capacitors are in parallel. From the text, C1 initially has 12 V and the switch is ideal; C2 is another ideal capacitor. Since there is no resistor or inductor in the pictured path, the circuit has no finite time constant or finite transient interval. The capacitors must reach their common parallel voltage instantaneously at t=0. Therefore i(t)=0 for t<0 and for t>0, with a nonzero singular current only at t=0: the current has the form of an impulse function.
